To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the difference in hexose content between two tomato fruit genotypes is independent of the rate of photoassimilates export from source leaves; (2) hexose transport across the plasma membranes of tomato fruit storage parenchymatous cells is the primary determinate of the difference in hexoses content between the two genotypes; and (3) the genotypic differences in hexose content are due to differences in the Vmax of the hexose carriers.
hexose carrier activity on the plasma membranes in the storage parenchyme of tomato fruit is the major determinant of the genotypically determined difference in sugar content of tomato fruit.

(1) the hexose carrier activity on the plasma membranes in storage parenchymal cells is a determinate factor in the genotypic differences in fruit hexose accumulation; (2) the genotypic variation in the carrier activity is not related to the activity of the carrier in the phloem; and (3) the genotypically determined differences in hexose carrier activity are due to differences in the carrier proteins and not to differences in the membrane energization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of sugar accumulation in developing tomato fruit.
the regulation of sugar transport and metabolism in the pericarp of tomato fruit.
the transport and transfer of sugars into developing tomato fruit and the regulation of sugar levels in the fruit.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hexose carriers of the plasma membrane are a major determinant of the rate of accumulation of sugars in the fruit of tomato, and the activity of these carriers is genetically controlled.
the genotypic differences in hexose accumulation are due to differences in hexose carrier activity in the storage parenchyme.
the genotypic differences in hexose accumulation in tomato fruit are determined by the activities of hexose carriers on energized membranes of the storage parenchymb cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the genotypic variation in hexose storage capacity is a function of the hexose carrier activity on the plasma membrane of the storage cells.
the hexose carrier activity of the storage parenchyme is a determinate for genotypic differences in hexose storage.
the genotypic differences in fruit sugar content of tomato are due to differences in the capacity of the storage parenchyme for hexose retrieval from the fruit apoplast.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hexose carrier activity in tomato fruit is a significant determinant of the genotypically controlled difference in hexose content.
